_meta.what: The squares and captions painted into the picture of the global map that go with places taken out of the game.
_meta.why: The full-scale map (res/globalmap/full/<n>.jpg, 273 tiles, one cell 8x8 pixels) has every place painted into the photograph itself: a coloured square on its cell and, for a few, a caption in letters. Hiding a place's name (data/map_labels.json) leaves its square, so a cut has to take the square off too.
_meta.rule: Every cell of data/retired.json 'cells' loses its square by itself: nothing to add here for a place that stood on a cell. 'cells' below are the other cells whose square goes -- a name with no place under it -- each with its why. 'captions' are letters painted into the picture, each as boxes of the map's pixels (x0, y0, x1, y1, inclusive; pixel = cell * 8) painted over whole. 'keep' lists cells whose name is hidden but whose square stays, each with its why: server/test_map_cells.py makes every hidden name with no live place under it be either here or erased.
_meta.how: server/map_cells.py finds each square in the picture and paints it over with the photograph's texture from near by; only the JPEG blocks it touches are encoded anew. client/build.py puts the edited tiles into every client release, bootstrap_http serves them on a local run. To look at the result: python3 server/map_cells.py --res <res> --preview <folder>.
